flawed_step: Step 3: From the valid local condition that every vertex has at least as many incident crossing edges as incident noncrossing edges, one cannot infer that the cut is globally maximum.
counterexample: Let G be the 6-cycle with vertices 1,2,3,4,5,6 and edges {12,23,34,45,56,61}. Take the partition A={1,2,4,5}, B={3,6}. Its crossing edges are 23,34,56,61, so its cut value is 4. Moving vertex 1, 2, 4, or 5 swaps one crossing edge with one noncrossing edge, leaving the value 4. Moving vertex 3 or 6 turns its two crossing edges into noncrossing edges, reducing the value to 2. Thus no single-vertex move strictly improves the cut. Nevertheless, the alternating partition A'={1,3,5}, B'={2,4,6} cuts all six edges and has value 6. Hence the locally unimprovable cut is not maximum.
assessment_summary: Step 1: Moving a vertex changes the cut value by its number of same-side neighbors minus its number of opposite-side neighbors. Step 2: Therefore single-vertex local optimality means every vertex has at least as many opposite-side as same-side neighbors. Both steps are justified. The required global conclusion does not follow, as the explicit C6 example shows.
